Backend: 5/5 pytest OK — beta_mode=false for apple-review-expired, beta_mode=true for apple-review-demo, /api/chantiers returns 402 subscription_expired for expired and 200 for active, /api/auth/me works for expired. Frontend web preview (Expo): after login with applereview-expired, PaywallScreen 'ACCÈS BLOQUÉ' displays IMMEDIATELY, ZERO 'Chargement impossible' alert fires, paywall persists >10s (no race condition), CONTACTER LE SUPPORT + SE DÉCONNECTER + S'ABONNER À PRO buttons all present, logout returns to /. Regression: applereview@mesurechassis.com loads dashboard normally (no paywall, no alert, chantiers list visible). Main agent should be aware that end-users on TestFlight/App Store get the fresh bundle, so this is a testing-environment quirk only.

rca_of_issue: Original Apple 2.1a rejection cause was 3-fold and all three are fixed: (1) routes/company.py:_to_profile returned beta_mode=true for every company including apple-review-expired, so AuthContext's condition `!company?.beta_mode` hid the PaywallScreen — fixed by `BETA_MODE and company_id != 'apple-review-expired'`. (2) src/services/api.ts response interceptor cleared the subscription lock on every successful (non-402) response, so /company/profile succeeding after login re-mounted the dashboard behind the paywall (race condition) — fixed by removing the success-branch clear. (3) dashboard.tsx (fetchData) and admin/stats.tsx (fetchData) unconditionally showed Alert.alert('Erreur','Chargement impossible.') on API failure — fixed with `if (status !== 402)` guards so the PaywallScreen is the ONLY UI shown on subscription-expired. All three fixes verified end-to-end via pytest + Playwright.
